faq.heading: Your questions, answered
faq.sub: Questions to resolve before committing to a property.

items.q: Can foreigners own property in the Dominican Republic?
items.a: Foreigners can generally acquire Dominican property without residence under the national-treatment framework. Confirm the exact title, ownership structure, coastal/public-domain, environmental and use restrictions with independent counsel.

items.q: What taxes do I pay when buying property?
items.a: The general real-estate transfer-tax rate is 3%, subject to the actual DGII basis and authorized relief. Individual-owner annual IPI generally applies at 1% above the annual exemption on combined taxable assessed holdings. Verify the year, owner structure and specific approvals; a CONFOTUR label is not automatic relief.

items.q: How long does the buying process take?
items.a: The schedule depends on documents, title and survey issues, financing, required approvals and registry processing. Agree evidence-based milestones; no fixed completion time is promised here.

items.q: Do I need a Dominican attorney?
items.a: Engage independent Dominican counsel, verify professional standing and conflicts, and agree the written scope. Ask who handles title, survey, seller authority, contract conditions, custody and registration; professional review does not guarantee every risk is removed.

items.q: What is residency and do I need it to buy property?
items.a: Buying and residence are separate processes. A purchase does not itself grant residence, extend a visitor stay or create blanket tax relief. Check current visa/residence requirements and any separately approved benefits for your circumstances.

items.q: Can I rent out my property when I'm not using it?
items.a: Confirm the property’s lawful rental use, association rules, permits, tax obligations, insurance and management arrangements before offering it. Do not assume that a listing or booking tool establishes rental permission or supports payment processing.
